roadmap_rows: | w2-agent-core follow-up 29 | **Controlled CPU contention does NOT reproduce the install overrun**: same-source quiet / loaded / quiet / loaded live + agent suites (Q2, Q3 / Q3r1 pass; L2 / L3 live pass with separately retained agent-test failures) plus six two-source interventions with host / container busy-loop workers up to 384 on 24 logical CPUs at 0 % idle — all 40 loaded Applies per intervention completed without a 100 ms overrun, maximum render→installed 53.133 ms (a 184.078 ms outer guard is a different measurement); the earlier correlation of overruns with chain-gate load (follow-up 28's 152 ms, isolation 10's 49 failed installs, members 11's generation-13 Applies) is **not** a causal conclusion and the historical cause stays unproven; the loaded meter / restart / expiry failures are retained, not diagnosed. **Additive TEST ONLY host context** around every Apply (`node/agent/measurement_host.go`: before / after samples — runnable queue, idle excluding iowait, load, unavailable samples explicit — plus sanitized returned command status), opt-in, outside the measured Apply operation, every existing row / sequence rule / D-106 digest input unchanged; producer audit validates 1,874 Apply host brackets. **Rollback is the node-wide baseline by design, not the previous generation**: a failed Apply closes every member (including the admitted sibling) until the next successful Apply; repeated failures keep the baseline indefinitely; the 100 ms bound is an install budget, not an outage ceiling; S2 observed a real sibling baseline drop after a successful Apply AND successful live verifier with a later `member_path_unconfigured` rejection — not the historical F11-03 mechanism, and proof that not every `verification_HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED` baseline means nft / tc verification failed; AT02's admitted positive control stays failed → the stronger admitted-sibling availability contract is an explicit enforcement design decision (**D-135**). No D-133 A/B invoked (no Apply / rollback ordering, timeout, policy or production forwarding change). Follow-up 28's four Sources links now point at the byte-identical `history/follow-up-9/` archive. Three requests: command-lifecycle evidence in `node/enforce/executor.go` / `apply.go` → netlab 22; the sibling availability contract → D-135; consumers label "fail-closed install overrun with recorded host contention" only when bounds and host samples support it, `cause_status=unproven` otherwise → members 12 / isolation 11. | done (#356) |

F18-01 documented as the intended D-125 negative 1 / 1 / 2. A first installer attempt aborted on the origin-slot .24 collision with the DNS third node — retained; the two campaigns run on separate reset stacks. D-102 answers for members 11 / updates 11 / dns-publish 9. One request: the F11-02 offline-installation paragraph (already corrected by updater 19, #351). | done (#352) |
